sections.history: Tirucheygnalur, today the village of Senganur beside the Manni river in the Thanjavur delta, is one of the old Shaiva shrines of Chola Nadu north of the Kaveri. Tirugnanasambandar sang of the Lord here in the Tevaram, which makes it a Paadal Petra Sthalam, and Sekkizhar's Periya Puranam names the village as the birthplace of Chandesvara Nayanar, one of the sixty-three Nayanmar saints. Temple tradition ties the first brick shrine to the early Chola king Kochengat Chola, a builder of the raised maadakkoil temples of this country; the present stone temple is attributed to the medieval Chola period, with later additions of the Vijayanagara age. The old place-name is read as Sei-nal-oor, the auspicious town of the divine child Murugan, and the shrine keeps the memory of a divine child and a devoted one.
sections.architecture: The temple faces east and is built as a maadakkoil, a shrine raised on a high base so that it seems to stand upon a hill; tradition says a fragment of Mount Meru fell here. There are two enclosures, one at the top and one at ground level. The sanctum holds the self-manifested linga of Sathyagireeswarar, and its doorway is narrow, a feature said to belong to the old elephant-proof temples. Unusually, the goddess Sakhi Devi is honoured in a shrine in the outer enclosure at ground level. In the maha mandapam stands a shrine of Bhairava, and the wall there is said to ring like bronze when tapped. The sacred waters include the Manni river beside the temple, the Sathya Pushkarini and the Kumara Theertham, and the shrine of Chandikeswarar draws special reverence.
sections.legends: The great legend of Senganur is Chandesvara's, told by Sekkizhar. In Seignalur lived a Brahmin couple, Echathathan and Pavithrai, whose son Visara Sarman mastered the Vedas while still a boy. Seeing a herdsman beat a calf, he asked to tend the village cattle himself, for he saw in the cows the Kamadhenu and a way to serve Shiva. On the bank of the Manni he shaped a linga of river sand and bathed it with the cows' milk. When a complaint reached his father, the father came to watch and, finding the boy lost in worship, kicked over the milk. Visara Sarman struck out with the staff in his hand; by the Lord's will it became an axe and cut his father's legs. Shiva and Parvati appeared, embraced the boy, and made him Chandesa, chief of the Lord's servants, which is why Chandikeswarar sits at the north of the sanctum in every Shiva temple. Local tradition also remembers Murugan receiving a divine weapon from his father here.
sections.festivals: The festival closest to the village's heart is the birthday of Chandesvara Nayanar, kept in Thai (January to February) on the Uthiram star. The temple also observes Avani Vinayaka Chaturthi, Aippasi Skanda Shashti and the Aippasi annabhishekam (October to November), Tirukarthikai (November to December) and Masi Maha Shivaratri (February to March). Confirm dates locally, as they follow the Tamil calendar.
sections.experience: Senganur is a small village in the quiet paddy country of the delta, and the temple is best visited in the calm of early morning or evening, when it is open. Climb to the hilltop sanctum of Sathyagireeswarar, then come down to the goddess Sakhi Devi in her shrine at ground level. Seek out the shrine of Chandikeswarar and remember that the saint honoured in every Shiva temple was born in this village. Tap the wall of the maha mandapam near Bhairava to hear it answer like bronze, and walk to the Manni river, where the boy is said to have bathed his sand linga with milk.

visit.timings: Reported as open for a short morning session, about 7:00 to 9:00 a.m., and again in the evening, about 5:30 to 7:00 p.m.; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer corridors and courtyards but prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals or priests.
visit.gettingThere: Senganur lies about 16 km from Kumbakonam on the road toward Chennai, in the Thiruvidaimarudur–Tirupanandal area. Kumbakonam is the main railway station and bus hub, and autos or taxis make the short onward run. The nearest airport is Tiruchirappalli, roughly 110 km away.
